bandReport.notes: 15 items, 49-63, no gaps, none spilling past a band edge. Item 49 opens at the top of p26-c1 with its number and full stem; item 63 closes on p32-c2 with a complete (d), so both edges are whole. TWO directions blocks fall in this band and both nest two passages. (1) p26-c2 'Directions for the following 4 (four) items' covers 51-54: Passage-1 (climate / agricultural disease, printed p26-c2) governs 51 and 52; Passage-2 (the statesman-and-opponents quotation, printed p28-c1 under the 'Passage - 2' heading) governs 53 and 54. Each item carries ONLY its own passage in `context`. (2) p32-c1 'Directions for the following 3 (three) items' covers 61-63: Passage-1 (corporate capitalism) governs 61 and 62 and is in their `context`; Passage-2 (the three-line 'network of voluntary associations' quotation) governs item 63 ALONE, so per section 6's rule of thumb (unique to one item = stem) it is transcribed at the head of item 63's STEM rather than in `context`, and 63 has no `context`. Flagging that as a judgement call: it is short quoted matter, it reads naturally inside the stem, and keeping it in the stem removes any chance of a hash collision. A human may move it to `context` if the merge prefers every directions-block item to carry one. COLLISION WATCH: items 52, 54 and 62 all end 'Which of the above assumptions is/are valid ?' and carry the identical four options (I only / II only / Both I and II / Neither I nor II); item 50 carries the same four options too. Their Statement I / Statement II text is what distinguishes them and is kept in the STEM in every case, so the four hashes are distinct. No data-sufficiency items appear in this band. COLUMN CROPS: p28-c2 and p32-c2 are both split a few pixels too far right - the item numbers are sheared off the left edge (p28-c2 shows '3.' and '.', p32-c2 shows '.' and '3.') and p32-c2 also clips the first character or two of two passage lines ('as a buffer' and 'individual'). questions.stem:
A mobile phone has been stolen. There are 3 suspects P, Q and R. They were questioned knowing that only one of them is guilty. Their responses are as follows :
P : I did not steal. Q stole it.
Q : R did not steal. I did not steal.
R : I did not steal. I do not know who did it.
Who stole the mobile phone ?
questions.subject: General Mental Ability

questions.stem:
Three teams P, Q, R participated in a tournament in which the teams play with one another exactly once. A win fetches a team 2 points and a draw 1 point. A team gets no point for a loss. Each team scored exactly one goal in the tournament. The team P got 3 points, Q got 2 points and R got 1 point. Which of the following statements is/are correct ?
I. The result of the match between P and Q is a draw with the score 0 – 0.
II. The number of goals scored by R against Q is 1.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.subject: Logical Reasoning and Analytical Ability

questions.context: It is hard to predict how changes in the climate and the atmosphere’s chemistry will affect the prevalence and virulence of agricultural diseases. But there is a risk that such changes will make some plant infections more common in all climatic zones, perhaps catastrophically so. Part of the problem is that centuries of selective breeding have refined the genomes of most high-value crops. They are spectacular at growing in today’s conditions but genetic variations that are not immediately useful to them have been bred out. This is good for yields but bad for coping with changes. A minor disease or even an unknown one could suddenly rampage through a genetically honed crop.
questions.stem: Which one of the following statements best reflects the central idea conveyed by the passage ?

options.label: A
options.text: Global climate change adversely affects the productivity of crops.

options.label: B
options.text: Our total dependence on genetically honed crops entails possible food insecurity.

options.label: C
options.text: Our food security should not depend on agricultural productivity alone.

options.label: D
options.text: Genetically honed crops should be replaced with their wild varieties in our present cultivation practices.

questions.subject: Comprehension

questions.context: “A good statesman, like any other sensible human being, learns more from his opponents than from his fervent supporters. For his supporters will push him to disaster unless his opponents show him where the dangers are. So if he is wise he will often pray to be delivered from his friends, because they will ruin him. But, though it hurts, he ought also to pray never to be left without opponents; for they keep him on the path of reason and good sense. The national unity of free people depends upon a sufficiently even balance of political power to make it impracticable for the administration to be arbitrary and for opposition to be revolutionary and irreconcilable.”
questions.stem: Which one of the following statements best reflects the critical message conveyed by the author of the passage ?

options.label: A
options.text: Without opposition parties, the administration in a democracy gets to become more responsible.

options.label: B
options.text: Democracy needs to have revolutionaries in opposition to keep the government alert.

options.label: C
options.text: Rulers in a democracy need the support of opposition for their political survival.

options.label: D
options.text: In a democracy, the opposition is indispensable for the balance of political power and good governance.

questions.context: There has been no democracy that has grown economically without corporate capitalism. It helps in modernizing the economy and enabling the transition from rural to urban, and agriculture to industry and services, which are inevitable with growth. It generates jobs — and there is no other way to fix a country’s unemployment challenge without a further impetus to private business. Big companies can operate on a large scale and become competitive both domestically and externally. A vibrant corporate capitalist base also leads to additional revenues for the State — which in turn, can be used for greater welfare for the marginalized and creating a more level playing field in terms of opportunities.
questions.stem: Which one of the following statements best reflects the critical message conveyed by the author of the passage ?

options.label: A
options.text: Corporate capitalism is important for economic growth of a State and also for democracy.

options.label: B
options.text: Corporate capitalism is imperative for a modern State to achieve its political objectives.

options.label: C
options.text: No State can ensure its economic survival for long without the role of corporate capitalism.

options.label: D
options.text: Corporate capitalism and democracy have mutual dependence for their continued existence.
